label: Painless elbow swelling
note: The patient presented with left elbow swelling noticed a week ago. The area was warm and felt fluid-filled but not painful. A history of osteoarthritis was confirmed by a GP previously. The patient has a peanut allergy. Examination revealed dry skin on the elbow tip. The patient was diagnosed with bursitis. Ibuprofen 400mg twice daily was prescribed. Blood tests for inflammatory markers and gout were arranged. A follow-up appointment was scheduled to review results. The patient was advised to return immediately if the elbow became red or very painful.
patient:
Your appointment today
You came because your left elbow swelled. It felt warm and held fluid but did not hurt. We checked your skin and found it was dry.

Your diagnosis
We suspect you have bursitis. This means the fluid bag at your elbow joint is inflamed.

Your treatment and next steps
Take Ibuprofen 400mg twice daily. Rest your elbow to help it heal. We will send blood tests to check for inflammation and gout. You must come back to see us soon to review the results.

When to contact us
Call us immediately if your elbow turns red. Call us immediately if your elbow becomes very painful.
summary: A patient in their fifties presented with a one-week history of painless, warm, fluid-filled swelling on the left elbow without trauma. Examination confirmed visible swelling with fluid fluctuation and dry skin. The working diagnosis was olecranon bursitis, managed with ibuprofen and blood tests sent to the patient’s home.

answers.happened: A painless, warm swelling over the elbow with no injury: bursitis on the picture, but the patient's real question was whether it was dangerous, and he asked it plainly. The safety-netting for an infected joint had frightened him more than the swelling had.
answers.learned: Describing the worst case before saying it is unlikely lands as a warning, not reassurance. Say what it is first, then what to watch for, and check how it was heard.
answers.next: I would give the diagnosis and the plan before the red flags, and book the follow-up as an appointment rather than contact us after the bloods, which leaves the next step with the patient.
